metadata.compilation_notes: Protocol compiled from Wu, W.-B. and Huang, J.-M., J. Org. Chem. 2014, 79, 10189-10195, DOI 10.1021/jo5018537. The MAIN general procedure (General Procedures for Electrochemical Reductive Cleavage of Aryl Ethers) was compiled: diphenyl ether (0.5 mmol) + NaBH4 (1.5 mmol) in 5 mL NMP with 0.2 M NaBF4, Pt foil anode (1x1.5 cm2) + Pt minigrid cathode (52 mesh, 1x1.5 cm2, 4 pieces), constant current 30 mA, 105 min, ambient temp. Workup: add n-tetradecane internal standard, pour into ice water, quench 1 M HCl at 0 C, extract (3x20 mL diethyl ether), dry Na2SO4, GC/GC-MS. Note that substrate preparation (Cu-catalyzed coupling, PBr3 benzyl bromination) is NOT the compiled protocol but documented separately. No blocking missing fields -> overall_status 'needs_review'. Ambient temperature (25 C) is an inferred quantity. Protocol ID assigned MF-REAL-004.

safety_checks.message: NaBH4 releases flammable hydrogen gas upon contact with water or moisture. Keep reagent dry and sealed; handle in fume hood and avoid open ignition sources. Account for slow H2 release during the 105 min electrolysis and workup.

ACID QUENCH RISK: Acidifying with 1 M HCl in the presence of residual NaBH4 produces vigorous, rapid hydrogen evolution. MUST add 1 M HCl very slowly with stirring at 0 C to control foaming and spatter and to prevent flammable H2 accumulation in the hood.
NMP (N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone) is a suspected reproductive toxicant (CMR) and skin irritant. Handle in fume hood with gloves and protective clothing; ensure minimal exposure.

Diethyl ether is extremely flammable (flash point -45 C) and a peroxide former. Perform extraction in a fume hood away from ignition sources; use fresh/industrial-grade ether and peroxide test indicator strips if old.
1 M HCl is corrosive/irritant. Wear impermeable gloves and goggles; quench at 0 C in an ice bath to reduce spatter.

During electrolysis, NaBH4 decomposition and possible cathodic H2 evolution generate flammable hydrogen. Ensure the fume hood/ventilation is active, no ignition source is nearby, and gas can escape freely. A deband unit / open-top cell is recommended.

Note: THF (flash point -14 C) and other low-boiling solvents were tested (Table 1) but give only trace product; the compiled protocol uses NMP solvent (nonflammable high bp 202 C). Do NOT substitute fused THF for NMP, which would raise flammability and lower borohydride solubility. Informational only.
Ambient temperature is quantified as 25 C (inferred). Confirm/set the working temperature band (typically 20-30 C) before the 105 min electrolysis, since reaction yields are temperature-sensitive.

recovery_policy.notes: If electrolysis is interrupted, record elapsed time and remaining duration; evaluate whether to resume or restart. NaBH4 solution should be re-quenched if store problem.

checkpoints.description: Quench completion (acidification done, no active H2 foaming)
